channel.title: MIA — Management Intelligence Alert
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: The Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% on 7 October, its first increase in nearly four years, in a unanimous vote, and its Monetary Policy Committee changed its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening by a majority.
item.description:
The decision follows a rise in headline consumer inflation from 4.5% in July to 4.8% in August, above the RBI's 4% medium-term target for a third consecutive month, and GDP growth of 7.8% in the first quarter of fiscal 2026–27, The Hindu Business Line and Business Recorder report. The RBI raised its growth forecast for fiscal 2026–27 from 6.7% to 7.1%, The Economic Times reports. Nearly 60% of economists in a Reuters poll had expected a 25 basis point increase, Business Recorder reports. The rupee ended 0.4% lower at 96.7750 per dollar on the day, after touching 96.8450, close to its record low of 96.96 of 20 May, with traders saying the policy was not hawkish enough to support the currency, Business Recorder reports. The reporting does not give the RBI's inflation forecast or the expected path of further increases.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The increase comes with a stance changed to calibrated tightening and what Business Recorder calls signals about further tightening, and the rupee weakened on the day. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, higher borrowing costs bear first on housing and vehicle finance, while a weaker rupee raises the cost of imported raw materials in India. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, India's construction and automotive demand and the cost of imported inputs are the two channels. Points that may be worth considering include the RBI's next decisions, the rupee's path, and whether vehicle and housing demand respond.

The Hindu Business Line | Business Recorder | The Economic Times | Business Recorder

item.title: Trade ministers of fifteen economies, including the US, the EU, Germany, France, India and Japan, signed a US-led joint statement calling on all countries to end non-market policies that perpetuate structural excess production and capacity.
item.description:
The statement followed G20 trade ministers' discussions in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on 30 September and 1 October, The Economic Times reports. The signatories are Argentina, Australia, Canada, the European Union, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Poland, Turkey, the United Kingdom and the United States, MarketScreener and The Economic Times report. The statement expresses the countries' resolve to work together in dedicated sectoral platforms to examine and take effective actions against structural excess production and capacity in several key sectors of concern, according to the USTR. The reporting does not name the sectors of concern, the measures envisaged, or the countries that did not sign.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The statement is a declaration of intent, not a trade measure; the reporting names no sector of concern, target country or instrument. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a shared statement on excess capacity can prepare the ground for coordinated trade defence in sectors such as steel, chemicals or vehicles, where overcapacity has been the stated reason for duties. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, coordinated action in chemical sectors would affect the price and origin of imported raw materials. Points that may be worth considering include which sectors the platforms take up first, whether trade defence actions follow, and the response of countries that did not sign.

Office of the US Trade Representative | MarketScreener | The Economic Times
item.source: Office of the US Trade Representative

item.title: The German government has blocked the sale of an 80% stake in Hamburg-based logistics company Zippel to Chinese state-owned shipping group Cosco on security grounds, saying it would have deepened dependencies and endangered supply-chain resilience.
item.description:
The decision was taken in the federal cabinet on Wednesday without further debate, according to Handelsblatt information from government circles. The economy ministry said the acquisition would have deepened dependencies and jeopardised the resilience of German and EU supply chains, Süddeutsche Zeitung and MarketScreener report. Zippel specialises in container logistics in the hinterland, connecting the North Sea ports with industrial and commercial centres in eastern Germany, has a capacity of 175,000 standard containers a year and a share of between 35% and 90% of throughput at the terminals in Berlin, Schkopau and Elsterwerda, Handelsblatt reports. It has about 350 employees, and more than 3,000 trains a year carry sea containers on its network from the terminals to the hinterland, Tagesschau reports. Cosco already holds a 24.99% stake in the Hamburg container terminal Tollerort, Süddeutsche Zeitung reports. The reporting does not give the price, Cosco's response, or whether other bidders exist.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The ban concerns one company; the grounds given are dependencies and supply-chain resilience, and the reporting does not give the deal's price. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, screening that treats inland logistics as critical widens the range of assets on which Chinese investment can be blocked in Germany. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, container rail links between the ports and eastern German industrial sites such as Schkopau are part of the supply route for chemical raw materials and finished goods. Points that may be worth considering include whether Cosco challenges the decision, who acquires Zippel instead, and whether further transactions are blocked on similar grounds.

Handelsblatt | Tagesschau | Süddeutsche Zeitung | MarketScreener

item.title: EU–China trade talks open in Beijing on 8 October, and China has reportedly rejected an EU proposal to limit hybrid car exports voluntarily to around 15% of the EU market, Commercial Times reports.
item.description:
EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič travels to Beijing for talks on 8–9 October, Dünya reports, with Commerce Minister Wang Wentao, according to Commercial Times. According to Commercial Times, the EU had proposed that China reduce its share from the current one-third of the EU market to around 15%, or face punitive measures including tariffs; after China's reported rejection, the EU is discussing an interim safeguard under which a limited number of Chinese hybrids could enter and any excess would face high additional tariffs. Commercial Times, citing insiders, also reports that the EU aims to set the limit low enough to avoid triggering Chinese retaliation, and that similar measures may be extended to other industries where the EU perceives trade imbalances. Shipments of hybrid cars from China to Europe reached around 50,000 in July 2026, up from around 3,800 a month in October 2024, Dünya reports. The Guardian reports that the negotiators hope for a pilot agreement in one sector, expected to be cars, before EU leaders meet in Brussels. The reporting does not give the proposed tariff rate or quota volume; Commercial Times names Valdis Dombrovskis rather than Šefčovič as the commissioner meeting Wang.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The talks are in progress; the rejection and the interim safeguard are reported by one outlet and no measure has been adopted. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a quota with high tariffs above it caps import volume rather than setting a price, which tends to shift some demand to European-built vehicles. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, any shift of vehicle assembly towards Europe would move bonding and sealing demand with it, and an extension to other sectors could reach chemical products. Points that may be worth considering include the outcome of the Beijing talks, the quota level if a safeguard is proposed, and which other sectors the EU names.

Commercial Times | Dünya Gazetesi | Commercial Times | The Guardian

item.title: The Critical Chemicals Alliance, established by the European Commission with industry groups, holds its general assembly on 8 October; Cefic figures show Europe's share of the global chemicals market fell from 23% to 13% between 2008 and 2024.
item.description:
Over the same period China's share rose from 19% to 46%, while the global market expanded in value from USD 2 trillion to USD 5 trillion, according to the European industry association Cefic, Hürriyet Daily News reports. The reporting does not give the alliance's agenda, the list of chemicals it treats as critical, the support measures under discussion, their conditions or cost, or any decisions expected from the assembly. It rests on one source.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The figures are market shares in a market that more than doubled in value, so Europe's 13% in 2024 is a smaller share of a larger market and does not by itself show a fall in European sales. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, an alliance that names critical chemicals tends to steer support and trade protection towards those products, which can change the availability and price of the molecules concerned in Europe. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, many formulations depend on European-produced intermediates, so the list of chemicals the alliance treats as critical matters for supply security. Points that may be worth considering include the outcome of the general assembly, which chemicals the alliance prioritises, and what conditions are attached to support.

Hürriyet Daily News

item.title: Sales of the office and contract furniture industry in Germany fell 5.6% year on year to around EUR 718 million in the first half of 2026, with domestic sales down 8.5% and foreign sales up 5.0%, according to the industry association IBA.
item.description:
The figures come from the Industrieverband Büro und Arbeitswelt (IBA), Initiative Mittelstand reports. Monthly sales rose 7.8% in June 2026. The reporting does not give the comparison basis for the June figure, the split between office and contract furniture, volumes rather than sales values, price effects, or the association's outlook for the second half. It rests on one source.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The figures are sales values for one segment over a half-year; the June rise is a single month and its comparison basis is not given. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, demand for office furniture follows office construction, refurbishment and office employment. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, furniture production uses edge-banding, laminating and assembly adhesives, so lower domestic furniture sales reduce that demand in the German home market. Points that may be worth considering include the second-half figures, whether the June increase continues, and how office construction and refurbishment in Germany develop.

Initiative Mittelstand

item.title: The Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors' house price balance fell to minus 32 in September from minus 28 in August, with buyer enquiries at minus 22 and agreed sales at minus 18, with economic uncertainty and higher borrowing costs cited as factors.
item.description:
The measure of buyer enquiries fell to minus 22 from minus 18 and the measure of agreed sales to minus 18 from minus 16, The Financial Times reports, with economic uncertainty and higher borrowing costs cited as factors. MarketScreener reports that the number of new properties coming onto the market rose for the first time since mid-2025 and that the fall in the price balance was driven by the prospect of higher interest rates. Lloyds data show UK house prices unchanged in September on the month and on the year, after their first annual fall since 2023 in August, and down 0.2% on the quarter, MarketScreener reports, with an average price of GBP 298,441, according to The Guardian; Lloyds noted that new enquiries from prospective mortgage borrowers were coming in at the fastest pace since February. The reporting does not give housing starts, construction activity or mortgage approvals.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The RICS figures are balances rather than prices or volumes, while Lloyds measures prices; the two point the same way on prices but differ on enquiries. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, weaker sales and prices tend to reduce housebuilding and the renovation that follows house moves, with a lag. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, UK demand for construction and renovation adhesives and sealants follows that activity. Points that may be worth considering include whether housing starts weaken in the coming months, how the Bank of England's rate path develops, and whether rising supply of homes for sale eases prices further.

The Financial Times | MarketScreener | MarketScreener | The Guardian

item.title: New passenger car registrations rose 12% in September 2026 to 156,629, with electric cars at 65,243 units, a 42% market share, up 108%, Le Dauphiné Libéré reports.
item.description:
Since the beginning of 2026 the cumulative total stands at 1,234,945 units, up 4%, Le Dauphiné Libéré reports. Electric car sales in the year to date total 387,338 units, a 31% market share, up 79%. Gasoline-LPG cars rose 23% to 5,234 units, a 3% market share. The reporting does not give hybrid, petrol or diesel figures, the period against which the changes are measured, the country covered by the figures, the reasons for the September increase, the share of French-built vehicles, or the publishing body of the figures. It rests on one source.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The figures are registrations in one month and the year to date; the 12% rise in September compares with a 4% rise in the year to date; the reporting does not state the comparison period for either. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, a 42% electric share in one month shows a market where battery-electric vehicles are a large part of new demand, although registrations measure sales, not production. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, the mix of drivetrains in sales shifts demand towards bonding, sealing and thermal-management materials used in electric vehicles. Points that may be worth considering include whether the September pace continues in the fourth quarter, the share of hybrids, and the origin of the vehicles sold.

Le Dauphiné Libéré

item.title: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron have agreed a common position to soften the EU's planned 2035 car CO2 target further than the Commission's proposal, which would cut the required reduction from 100% to 90%.
item.description:
Under current EU law, adopted in 2023 according to Bild, average CO2 emissions of new cars would have to fall by 100% by 2035 compared with 2021, which would de facto end the combustion engine, Handelsblatt reports; the Commission proposed in December 2025, under pressure from Germany, to lower the target to 90%, with manufacturers able to offset the remaining 10% through low-CO2 European steel, e-fuels and biofuels. According to Bild, Merz and Macron want another ten percentage points dropped without compensation, mathematically to 80%, and want manufacturers to be given five years instead of three to meet the 2030 interim target. Bild cites experts who say that even under the Commission's proposal around 27% to 29% of new registrations could still have a combustion engine after 2035. El Correo reports that Macron gives up his opposition to relaxing fleet limits, while Merz accepts the French demand for more guarantees that European public money favours manufacturers and components produced in Europe. The reporting does not give a timetable or the positions of other member states and the European Parliament.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The position is a joint proposal by two governments, not a change in EU law. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, such a change would need agreement in the EU legislative process, and a lower 2035 target and five years instead of three to meet the 2030 target would keep combustion and hybrid drivetrains in European production for longer, alongside electric vehicles, while a European-content preference ties public money to where components are made. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, a longer mixed drivetrain period means carmakers keep sourcing both the materials used in combustion vehicles and those used in battery-electric vehicles. Points that may be worth considering include whether other member states join the position, how the European Parliament responds, and how the European-preference guarantees are defined.

Handelsblatt | Bild | El Correo

item.title: Production in Germany rose 2% in August 2026 from July, according to the Federal Statistical Office, mainly because construction output increased 9.3%, while automotive production fell 5.4% and chemical production 1.2%.
item.description:
Industrial production in the narrow sense, excluding energy and construction, rose 0.6% in August from July, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung reports. Within manufacturing, mechanical engineering rose 5.3%, while the automotive industry fell again. Chemical production fell 1.2% in August, seasonally and calendar-adjusted, after a decline of 3.2% in July. MarketScreener reports that the construction increase came particularly from specialised construction and finishing trades, as well as from the manufacturing of machinery and equipment. The reporting does not give the year-on-year changes, the July figure for the overall index, the breakdown of construction between building and civil engineering, or any revision to earlier months, and Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung and MarketScreener label the 2% measure differently, as manufacturing-sector production and as industrial production.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The 2% rise rests mainly on construction; industry excluding energy and construction rose 0.6%, and automotive and chemical output fell, so the sectors moved in different directions, with mechanical engineering up 5.3%. On a general reading rather than on anything in the sources, a single strong month in construction can reflect weather and timing, and finishing trades are the stage of construction closest to interior materials. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, finishing work uses flooring adhesives, sealants and tile adhesives, while the continued fall in automotive output weighs on bonding demand in vehicle assembly. Points that may be worth considering include whether the construction gain holds in September, how construction orders develop, and whether automotive output stabilises.

Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung | MarketScreener

item.title: Russian diesel production fell more than 23% year on year and crude processing to 3.8 million barrels a day, around 30% below its level before the outbreak of the conflict, after Ukraine intensified drone strikes on refineries, China Economic Net reports.
item.description:
Ukraine has intensified deep drone strikes against Russian refineries over the past 18 months, severely damaging Russian refining capabilities, China Economic Net reports; according to the latest IEA data, Russian refineries were attacked at least 22 times in August, the highest number in a single month since the outbreak of the conflict. Gasoline production fell 20% year on year, and the fall in output prompted the Russian government to restrict fuel exports to ensure domestic supply. The reporting does not give the month to which the 3.8 million barrel and production figures refer, the scope and duration of the export restrictions, the volumes of diesel Russia still exports, or which markets are most affected. It rests on one source.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The 30% fall compares crude processing with the period before the conflict, while the diesel and gasoline declines are year-on-year changes, so the figures measure different periods. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, Russia has been a large exporter of refined products, and lower runs with export restrictions remove diesel from a market where other refining capacity is also disrupted. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, tighter diesel supply reaches distribution and energy costs, and lower refinery runs can affect availability of refinery-derived feedstocks. Points that may be worth considering include whether the export restrictions are extended, the pace of strikes on refineries, and how far other suppliers replace Russian diesel.

China Economic Net

item.title: BASF chief executive Markus Kamieth said at the Handelsblatt and WirtschaftsWoche Germany Summit in Berlin that the chemical industry faces a large wave of takeovers and mergers, and that BASF as market leader wants to seize its opportunities.
item.description:
A few weeks ago BASF submitted a takeover bid of around EUR 10 billion for its Essen-based competitor Evonik, which Evonik's board of directors rejected, Handelsblatt reports. Kamieth did not specifically address the offer to Evonik on the podium. He justified the interest in takeovers with industrial logic: a combination of BASF and another strong player from specialty chemicals makes a lot of sense, he said, and in such a combination BASF could contribute its strength in basic chemicals. Handelsblatt describes Evonik as number two in Germany after BASF, focused on lucrative specialty chemical products. The reporting does not say whether BASF intends to renew or raise its offer, which other companies or segments Kamieth has in view, what is driving the wave he expects, or how Evonik's shareholders have responded. It rests on one source.

Potential Industry Impact (AI-Assessed)

The statement is the view of a company that describes itself as market leader, not a transaction; the one reported bid was rejected. On a general reading rather than on anything in the source, a combination of basic and specialty chemistry links commodity feedstocks with formulated products, and consolidation of that kind tends to change who supplies specialty raw materials and on what terms. On the same general reading, for adhesive technologies, specialty chemical producers supply many of the additives, resins and intermediates used in formulations, so a wave of mergers among them could alter supplier choice and negotiating positions. Points that may be worth considering include whether BASF returns with a revised offer for Evonik, whether other European producers announce combinations, and how competition authorities treat overlaps in specialty chemicals.

Handelsblatt
